tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__add_repo
tools.description:
Add a GitHub repository to the current session so you can read, clone, or operate on it alongside the repos already in the session. Call this whenever you need a repository the session does not have — including when someone only asks a question about one, rather than asking for it to be attached. Prefer attaching a repository over reporting that you cannot reach it. 

IMPORTANT — DO NOT PRE-CHECK THE REPO BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL. Do not curl github.com, do not run `gh repo view`, do not run `git ls-remote` to verify the repo exists. Unauthenticated requests to private repos return 404 ("Not Found") even when the repo is real and your session has authorized access to it. Those preemptive 404s will mislead you into skipping the tool. Instead: call add_repo with the owner/repo exactly as you have it. The backend performs the real reachability + authorization check and returns a structured error you can act on. If the repo genuinely doesn't exist or isn't accessible, the tool response will tell you — report that to the user. If it does exist, the tool response will include a clone command you can then run. Do not report success until the tool has actually been called and returned. 

WHEN ACCESS IS DENIED: if the tool returns an authorization or policy error — the repo exists but isn't enabled for this workspace/project/organization, or the GitHub App isn't installed or linked — relay the tool's exact reason to the user. The response names the remedy: if Claude doesn't have GitHub access for this organization at all, the user should reconnect GitHub under claude.ai Settings → Connectors; if the repo is simply not in the allowed set, a Claude.ai organization owner can grant access in the settings page the response points to. Do not add settings URLs beyond those provided here or in the tool response. Do not retry the same repo. You may remind the user which repositories are already available in this session, and offer to help them request access. Do not guess, infer, or list repositories you cannot see in the tool res… [truncated]

access.description: What access this session needs. "read" (default): fetch/clone only — when the repository is public, git read access is often already served by the session's git proxy with nothing to attach, and the tool says so instead of attaching. "push": the session must push commits, open PRs, or use GitHub API tools against the repository, so it is attached with credentials after the full repository-access checks.

owner.description: GitHub owner (user or organization) of the repo to add, e.g. "anthropics".

repo.description: GitHub repo name, e.g. "claude-code". Do not include the owner prefix — pass owner and repo as separate fields.

tools.description: Archive a Claude Code Remote session. Transitions the session to read-only archived state and releases its container. Use this when a child session has finished its work or is stuck (PR merged, task complete, session failed to initialize) and a human has already acknowledged they're done with the session.

session_id.description: The target session ID to archive.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session
tools.description: Create a new Claude Code Remote session. Returns the new session's ID and status. If environment_id is omitted, the new session inherits the calling session's environment. Combine with send_message for fan-out orchestration: spawn a sibling and send it a task. Where enabled, this session receives a <child-session-event> turn if the new session's turn fails or its worker restarts and drops background tasks; a session that finishes cleanly does not report back, so check on it with get_session (status_bucket reads 'failed' for a turn that errored, where status alone reads 'idle' either way) and list_events.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session
schema.description: Create a new Claude Code Remote session. Returns the new session's ID and status. If environment_id is omitted, the new session inherits the calling session's environment. Combine with send_message for fan-out orchestration: spawn a sibling and send it a task. Where enabled, this session receives a <child-session-event> turn if the new session's turn fails or its worker restarts and drops background tasks; a session that finishes cleanly does not report back, so check on it with get_session (status_bucket reads 'failed' for a turn that errored, where status alone reads 'idle' either way) and list_events.

append_system_prompt.description: Text appended to the new session's system prompt.

environment_id.description: Environment ID — a tagged ID starting with 'env_' (or 'ccpool_' for self-hosted pools). Defaults to the calling session's environment. Do NOT invent a value — call list_environments to get the user's real environment_ids. When this resolves to the remote_cowork environment (explicitly or via inheritance), a Claude Cowork session is spawned — the account's enabled skills, plugins and the Cowork system prompt are assembled server-side, and only prompt, title, model and tags are read (source_url, extra_allowed_tools, append_system_prompt and environment_variables are ignored so the caller cannot widen the tool surface).

extra_allowed_tools.description: Extra tool names pre-approved without a user permission prompt. Entries the calling session does not itself have pre-approved are dropped — the child never carries a grant its parent lacks.

model.description: Model ID for the new session. Defaults to the calling session's model.

outcome_branch.description: Optional branch name to push changes to. When set, the session pushes directly to this branch (no session-derived suffix appended).

permission_mode.description: Initial permission mode for the new session. Cannot be more permissive than the calling session's mode; omit to inherit it. 'plan' makes the agent propose a plan and then BLOCKS waiting for human approval via the claude.ai/code web UI — do NOT use 'plan' for autonomous child sessions that no human is watching, as they will stall indefinitely at the approval prompt.

prompt.description: Optional initial message to send to the new session.

source_revision.description: Optional git branch, tag, or commit to check out. Requires source_url. Defaults to the repo's default branch.

source_url.description: Optional git repository URL to check out.

tags.description: Free-form tags to categorize the session (e.g. ["remote-agents-project:frontend"]). Editable later via set_session_tags.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger
tools.description: Create a Routine (scheduled trigger). Three targeting modes: (1) default — fires into THIS SESSION, resuming the same conversation each time; (2) persistent_session_id set — fires into a SPECIFIC OTHER SESSION you name (must be in your account); (3) create_new_session_on_fire=true — spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing. Use mode 1 for recurring work you want to pick back up yourself; mode 2 for waking a sibling session you created; mode 3 when each firing should start from a clean slate. If the result warns that the Routine stores no connectors, say so plainly when you confirm the Routine to the user and pass on the remedy it names; never report such a Routine as simply created.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger
schema.description: Create a Routine (scheduled trigger). Three targeting modes: (1) default — fires into THIS SESSION, resuming the same conversation each time; (2) persistent_session_id set — fires into a SPECIFIC OTHER SESSION you name (must be in your account); (3) create_new_session_on_fire=true — spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing. Use mode 1 for recurring work you want to pick back up yourself; mode 2 for waking a sibling session you created; mode 3 when each firing should start from a clean slate. If the result warns that the Routine stores no connectors, say so plainly when you confirm the Routine to the user and pass on the remedy it names; never report such a Routine as simply created.

connectors.description: Optional list of connector names the Routine's fired sessions may use, e.g. ["Gmail", "linear"]. Pass ONLY connectors the user explicitly asked this Routine to use — the stored grant applies to every future firing. Names resolve against the user's connected claude.ai connectors; when calling from inside a CCR session the list is further limited to connectors that session itself holds (it can only narrow that set, never widen it). Any name that cannot be resolved fails the call. Pass [] to store no connectors. Omit to keep the default behavior for this surface. The grant attaches the connectors only — individual tool calls from fired sessions still go through runtime permission checks.

create_new_session_on_fire.description: If true, each firing creates a fresh session in the calling session's environment instead of resuming an existing one. Default false. Mutually exclusive with persistent_session_id.

cron_expression.description: Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), evaluated in UTC. Convert local times to UTC first, using the offset currently in effect. If the conversion crosses midnight, shift the day fields that are set, day-of-week and/or day-of-month (e.g. weekdays at 5pm in UTC-07:00 is 0 0 * * 2-6). Minimum interval is normally hourly (some projects allow shorter); a too-frequent schedule is rejected and the error names the minimum. For hourly or every-N-hours schedules, use minute 0 (e.g. '0 * * * *', '0 */4 * * *'): the server anchors it to the creation minute ('hourly starting now'), so Routines spread across the hour instead of all firing at :00. All other schedules are stored verbatim. Mutually exclusive with run_once_at. Omit both for a poke-only Routine that never fires on its own schedule.

environment_id.description: Environment ID — a tagged ID starting with 'env_' (or 'ccpool_' for self-hosted pools). Defaults to the calling session's environment. Required when calling from outside a CCR session (no session context to inherit from). Do NOT invent a value — call list_environments to get the user's real environment_ids.

initiation.description: Who wanted this: human_request — a person asked you to set this up now; human_schedule — a schedule a person set (e.g. an earlier firing) told you to; own_followup — your own check-in or follow-up on work you are already doing; own_initiative — you decided on your own that this should exist.

notifications.description: Completion notifications for this Routine. push sends to the owner's phone when a run finishes with something noteworthy; email sends the same summary to their inbox. If omitted, the setting stays unset and the server default applies at fire time. Passing this sets an explicit per-Routine choice, so list every channel you want on ({push:true, email:true} for both; {email:true} alone means email-only, push off). Pass {} to opt out of all channels. Only fresh-session-per-fire Routines (create_new_session_on_fire=true) take this; the server rejects it for self-bind or persistent_session_id Routines.

persistent_session_id.description: Optional session ID to fire into instead of this one. Must belong to the same account — the server rejects sessions you don't own. Omit to fire into this session (default). Mutually exclusive with create_new_session_on_fire.

prompt.description: The message the Routine sends on each firing. When binding to an existing session (modes 1-2), write it assuming past context — the conversation continues. In fresh-session mode (mode 3), write it as a complete standalone instruction since each firing starts from nothing.

run_once_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp for a one-shot fire (e.g. 2026-04-20T17:00:00Z). Must be in the future. Mutually exclusive with cron_expression — set one or the other, not both. After the one-shot fires the Routine disables itself with ended_reason=run_once_fired.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__delete_trigger
tools.description: Delete a Routine (scheduled trigger). The Routine must belong to the calling session's account — deleting another account's Routine fails with not-found. Use this to undo a create_trigger call or to clean up Routines whose work is done. A bad cron or wrong prompt does not need deletion — update_trigger fixes those in place, keeping the Routine's run history. On success, the result usually echoes the deleted Routine's last state (including its name) in the response's trigger field — callers without stored-data read access get a plain-text confirmation instead. Either way the Routine no longer exists once this returns.

=================== reproducible-llm-template/README.md
# Reproducible-LLM research template

A drop-in harness that makes an LLM-assisted research repo fully
auditable: every prompt, every session, and every session transcript is
stored inside the repo and guarded by git hooks. Designed for Claude
Code; the log formats are tool-agnostic.

This folder lives at the root of this repository (it is repository-wide
infrastructure, not part of any one manuscript).

It is a *template*: copy its contents into the root of a fresh
repo (or a fresh `git init`), or — the intended path — publish it as a
GitHub template repository so new projects start from it with one click.
Alternatively, paste `INIT-PROMPT.md` into Claude Code in any repo and it
will build the system in place.

## The model

- **Prompt log** — `llm-log/prompt-log.csv`: one row per prompt
  (date, time, llm_model, username, prompt_text, session_id), appended in
  real time by a Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook.
- **Sessions** — `llm-log/sessions.csv`: one row per Claude Code session
  (start date, start time, session_id, source). Context windows are
  finite, so a project accumulates many sessions; this file is the index.
- **Transcripts** — `llm-log/transcripts/<session_id>.jsonl`: the full
  Claude Code session transcript (prompts, responses, tool calls, model
  ids, timestamps), copied into the repo by a `Stop` hook after every
  assistant turn (so the archived copy is always current, even if the
  session dies without a clean `SessionEnd` — important for ephemeral
  web/remote containers) and again on `SessionEnd`.
- **Git guard** — `githooks/pre-commit`: refuses/repairs commits where
  the working llm-log is out of sync (e.g. a transcript newer than its
  archived copy), and auto-stages `llm-log/` so LLM work and its
  provenance always land in the same commit.

## Contents

```
.claude/settings.json           # registers the hooks (committable)
.claude/hooks/capture-prompt.sh # UserPromptSubmit -> prompt-log.csv
.claude/hooks/session-start.sh  # SessionStart    -> sessions.csv
.claude/hooks/archive-transcript.sh # Stop + SessionEnd -> transcripts/
githooks/pre-commit             # git guard
setup.sh                        # one-time install (chmod, core.hooksPath)
INIT-PROMPT.md                  # the single Claude Code "init" prompt
```

## Install (manual)

```bash
cp -r <template>/. /path/to/your-repo/
cd /path/to/your-repo
./setup.sh          # chmod +x hooks, git config core.hooksPath githooks
git add -A && git commit -m "Add reproducible-LLM harness"
```

Set `PROMPT_LOG_USER="Your Name"` in your environment (or the Claude
Code web environment settings) so log rows carry the researcher's name.


## Session and manuscript convention (live in this repo since 2026-09-14)

The harness above is installed and active at the repo root (`.claude/
settings.json` + `.claude/hooks/`), logging to `llm-log/`. Rules:

- **One session = one manuscript.** Declare the manuscript in your first
  prompt (e.g. "M3: ..."). Do not mix manuscripts in one session.
- `llm-log/sessions.csv` has a `manuscript` column (`2`, `3`, `4`,
  `infra`, `mixed(...)`). New sessions are added automatically as
  `untagged` - tag them by editing the CSV, ideally the same day.
- **Publication export**: at publication of manuscript N, export the
  sessions tagged N (plus relevant `mixed`/`infra` sessions) with their
  transcripts to that manuscript's public flat repo.
- **Redaction is mandatory before any transcript goes public.** Sessions
  recorded before publication was planned (all manuscript 2 sessions)
  contain confidential material: peer-review content, editor/reviewer
  names, personal contact details. Publish only after a documented
  redaction pass. Manuscript 2's stream covers the revision phase only
  (2026-08-12 onward); its pre-submission sessions were never recorded.
- **Resumed sessions**: a session resumed in a fresh container rebuilds
  a smaller (compacted) transcript. The archive hook never overwrites a
  larger archive; the continuation lands in `<session_id>.resumed.jsonl`.
  Both parts belong to the session.
- `Manuscript3/prompt-log.csv` is the historical prompt log from before
  the central harness existed; the live log is `llm-log/prompt-log.csv`.


## What gets committed, and when

The hooks **never commit your work**. They only write into `llm-log/` and
stage it:

- `UserPromptSubmit` appends one row to `llm-log/prompt-log.csv`.
- `Stop` (after each assistant turn) refreshes the archived transcript and
  runs `git add llm-log` - staged, not committed.
- `SessionEnd` regenerates `llm-log/SESSIONS.md`, then commits **only**
  `llm-log/` (`git commit -o llm-log`) and pushes. One commit per session,
  not per prompt.

So: no commit per prompt, and a session that ends without anyone saying
"commit" still lands its log. Your manuscript and code changes are
committed the normal way, by you or by Claude during the session - the
log commit never sweeps them up.

Regenerate the human-readable index at any time with
`python3 llm-log/build-index.py`.

## Caveats

- Transcript JSONL is an internal Claude Code format and may change
  between versions; the prompt CSV is the stable, human-readable record.
- Transcripts can contain file contents and command output from your
  machine — only use in repos where that is acceptable to publish.
- `.git/hooks` is not versioned; that is why `setup.sh` uses
  `core.hooksPath` to point git at the committed `githooks/` folder.

# LLM session log - human-readable index

Generated by `llm-log/build-index.py` from the session transcripts in
`llm-log/transcripts/` and the index in `llm-log/sessions.csv`.
**Do not edit by hand** - regenerate instead.

Every prompt given to Claude Code in this repository, and the full
session transcript (prompts, replies, tool calls, file edits), is
stored in `llm-log/`. The `.jsonl` transcripts are the machine-readable
record and are named by session id; this file is the plain-language
guide to them. `llm-log/prompt-log.csv` lists every prompt with a
timestamp. See `reproducible-llm-template/README.md` for the design.

Sessions are tagged by manuscript: `2` = Epilepsia systematic review of
IED reproducibility, `3` = LLM phase-1 screening validation, `4` =
neonatal EEG reproducibility, `infra` = repository tooling.

> Note: transcripts recorded before publication was planned may contain
> confidential material (peer review, contact details). A documented
> redaction pass is required before any of this is published.

# Reproducible-LLM research template

A drop-in harness that makes an LLM-assisted research repo fully
auditable: every prompt, every session, and every session transcript is
stored inside the repo and guarded by git hooks. Designed for Claude
Code; the log formats are tool-agnostic.

This folder lives at the root of this repository (it is repository-wide
infrastructure, not part of any one manuscript).

It is a *template*: copy its contents into the root of a fresh
repo (or a fresh `git init`), or — the intended path — publish it as a
GitHub template repository so new projects start from it with one click.
Alternatively, paste `INIT-PROMPT.md` into Claude Code in any repo and it
will build the system in place.

## The model

- **Prompt log** — `llm-log/prompt-log.csv`: one row per prompt
  (date, time, llm_model, username, prompt_text, session_id), appended in

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a human-readable index of the LLM session log.

Reads llm-log/sessions.csv and llm-log/transcripts/*.jsonl and writes
llm-log/SESSIONS.md - a plain-text overview so that a person who checks
out this repository without access to an LLM can see what each session
did, when, and for which manuscript.

The JSONL transcripts remain the machine-readable ground truth; file
names keep their session-id form so automatic traceability is intact.
This index is derived - regenerate it with:

    python3 llm-log/build-index.py

import csv
import json
import os
import re
from datetime import datetime

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
LOG = os.path.join(ROOT, "llm-log")
TRANSCRIPTS = os.path.join(LOG, "transcripts")
MAXLEN = 160


def clean(text):
    """Collapse a prompt to a single readable line."""
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]{1,40}>", " ", text)          # strip xml-ish tags
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
    if len(text) > MAXLEN:
        text = text[: MAXLEN - 1].rstrip() + "…"
    return text


def read_transcript(path):
    """Return (prompts, first_ts, last_ts, models, tools) from a .jsonl."""
    prompts, models, tools = [], set(), {}
    first_ts = last_ts = None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        for line in f:
            try:
                obj = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            ts = obj.get("timestamp")
            if ts:
                first_ts = first_ts or ts
                last_ts = ts
            typ = obj.get("type")
            msg = obj.get("message") or {}
            if typ == "user":
                content = msg.get("content")
                if isinstance(content, str):
                    txt = content
                elif isinstance(content, list):
                    txt = " ".join(
                        c.get("text", "")
                        for c in content
                        if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "text"
                    )
                else:
                    txt = ""
                txt = txt.strip()
                # skip tool results, hook noise and system-injected turns
                if txt and not txt.startswith(("<", "Caveat:", "[Request interrupted")):
                    prompts.append((ts, clean(txt)))
            elif typ == "assistant":
                if msg.get("model"):
                    models.add(msg["model"])
                for c in msg.get("content", []) or []:
                    if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "tool_use":
                        name = c.get("name", "?")
                        tools[name] = tools.get(name, 0) + 1
    return prompts, first_ts, last_ts, models, tools


def duration(a, b):
    try:
        fmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"
        d1 = datetime.strptime(a[:19], fmt)
        d2 = datetime.strptime(b[:19], fmt)
        mins = int((d2 - d1).total_seconds() // 60)
        if mins < 60:
            return f"{mins} min"
        return f"{mins // 60} h {mins % 60} min"
    except Exception:
        return "?"


def main():
    sessions = []
    csv_path = os.path.join(LOG, "sessions.csv")
    if os.path.exists(csv_path):
        with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            sessions = list(csv.DictReader(f))

    known = {s.get("session_id") for s in sessions}
    for fn in sorted(os.listdir(TRANSCRIPTS)):
        if fn.endswith(".jsonl"):
            sid = fn[:-6].replace(".resumed", "")
            if sid not in known:
                sessions.append({"session_id": sid, "manuscript": "untagged",
                                 "start_date": "", "start_time": "", "source": ""})
                known.add(sid)

    out = []
    out.append("# LLM session log - human-readable index\n")
    out.append(
        "Generated by `llm-log/build-index.py` from the session transcripts in\n"
        "`llm-log/transcripts/` and the index in `llm-log/sessions.csv`.\n"
        "**Do not edit by hand** - regenerate instead.\n"
    )
    out.append(
        "Every prompt given to Claude Code in this repository, and the full\n"
        "session transcript (prompts, replies, tool calls, file edits), is\n"
        "stored in `llm-log/`. The `.jsonl` transcripts are the machine-readable\n"
        "record and are named by session id; this file is the plain-language\n"
        "guide to them. `llm-log/prompt-log.csv` lists every prompt with a\n"
        "timestamp. See `reproducible-llm-template/README.md` for the design.\n"
    )
    out.append(
        "Sessions are tagged by manuscript: `2` = Epilepsia systematic review of\n"
        "IED reproducibility, `3` = LLM phase-1 screening validation, `4` =\n"
        "neonatal EEG reproducibility, `infra` = repository tooling.\n"
    )
    out.append(
        "> Note: transcripts recorded before publication was planned may contain\n"
        "> confidential material (peer review, contact details). A documented\n"
        "> redaction pass is required before any of this is published.\n"
    )

    rows, details = [], []
    for s in sorted(sessions, key=lambda r: (r.get("start_date") or "", r.get("start_time") or "")):
        sid = s.get("session_id", "")
        parts = [p for p in (os.path.join(TRANSCRIPTS, sid + ".jsonl"),
                             os.path.join(TRANSCRIPTS, sid + ".resumed.jsonl"))
                 if os.path.exists(p)]
        prompts, first_ts, last_ts, models, tools = [], None, None, set(), {}
        size = 0

            prompts += pr
            first_ts = first_ts or f_ts
            last_ts = l_ts or last_ts

1. Which file(s) in biosig4c++/t210 handle Cadwell (likely sopen_cadwell_read.c). 2. The exact license of libbiosig / biosig4c++ (GPL-2.0-or-later? GPL-3.0-or-later?), quoting the license header of that file and the top-level LICENSE/COPYING.
3. Any documentation or changelog entries about Cadwell support (release notes, NEWS, mailing list posts, sourceforge tickets).
4. Whether there's an existing Python binding (pip "biosig") and whether the Cadwell reader is exposed via it, and any other open-source Cadwell readers you can find (MNE-Python? Neo? EDFbrowser? pyedflib? "cadwell" on GitHub/PyPI).
5. Licensing analysis: implications of porting GPL code into a public-domain repo (repo must relicense to GPL-compatible; recommended options), vs. clean-room reimplementation from format knowledge, vs. linking libbiosig as a dependency.

Be precise, cite URLs, and clearly mark anything you could not verify.

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

description.description: What needs to be done

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

description.description: New description for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. Exception: claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) ARE fetchable via your claude.ai login — use WebFetch, not curl (curl gets the SPA shell or a Cloudflare 403).
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is September 2026 — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""LLM session logger for this repository.

Every Claude Code session that touches this repository is archived under
``llm-logs/<session_id>/`` and indexed in ``llm-logs/sessions.csv``.  This
single script implements all the hook actions so the shell hooks in
``.claude/hooks/`` stay one-liners.

Sub-commands (each reads the Claude Code hook JSON payload on stdin
unless ``--transcript``/``--session-id`` are given explicitly):

  session-start   register the session in sessions.csv (SessionStart hook)
  prompt          append the submitted prompt to prompt-log.csv and to the
                  session's prompts.csv in real time (UserPromptSubmit hook)
  archive         copy the transcript into llm-logs/<session_id>/, rebuild
                  the session's human-readable files and the global index,
                  and ``git add llm-logs`` (Stop + SessionEnd hooks)
  commit          commit ONLY llm-logs/ and push to the current branch
                  (SessionEnd hook)
  index           rebuild llm-logs/SESSIONS.md and every session's
                  PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md from the archived transcripts

Layout of one session folder::

  llm-logs/<session_id>/
      transcript.jsonl              full Claude Code transcript (ground truth)
      transcript.resumed.jsonl      continuation, if the session was resumed
                                    in a fresh container (compacted transcript)
      session.json                  metadata: start/end, models, tools, branch
      prompts.csv                   one row per human prompt (from transcript)
      PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md      every prompt in full and the assistant's
                                    text replies, readable without an LLM

The transcript JSONL is an internal Claude Code format and may change; the
CSV and Markdown files are the stable, human-readable record.  Never edit
the generated files by hand - rerun ``python3 llm-logs/tools/llmlog.py index``.
"""
import csv
import datetime as dt
import getpass
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
LOG = os.path.dirname(HERE)                      # .../llm-logs
ROOT = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or os.path.dirname(LOG)
LOG = os.path.join(ROOT, "llm-logs")
SESSIONS_CSV = os.path.join(LOG, "sessions.csv")
PROMPT_LOG_CSV = os.path.join(LOG, "prompt-log.csv")
SESSIONS_HEADER = ["start_date", "start_time_utc", "session_id", "user",
                   "source", "git_branch", "prompts", "first_prompt", "topic"]
PROMPT_LOG_HEADER = ["date", "time_utc", "user", "session_id", "prompt_text"]
MAXLEN = 200
GENERATED_NOTE = "<!-- generated by llm-logs/tools/llmlog.py - do not edit, rerun `index` -->"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def now_utc():
    return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)


def username():
    return (os.environ.get("PROMPT_LOG_USER")
            or os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL")
            or getpass.getuser())


def source():
    if os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE"):
        return "claude-code-remote"
    return "claude-code"


def git(*args):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, check=False).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""


def read_payload(args):
    """Hook payload from stdin, merged with explicit command-line overrides."""
    data = {}
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        raw = sys.stdin.read()
        if raw.strip():
            try:
                data = json.loads(raw)
            except Exception:
                data = {}
    if args.session_id:
        data["session_id"] = args.session_id
    if args.transcript:
        data["transcript_path"] = args.transcript
    if not data.get("session_id"):
        data["session_id"] = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID", "")
    if not data.get("transcript_path") and data.get("session_id"):
        # Default Claude Code location: ~/.claude/projects/<mangled cwd>/<id>.jsonl
        mangled = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "-", ROOT)
        cand = os.path.expanduser(os.path.join("~", ".claude", "projects", mangled,
                                               data["session_id"] + ".jsonl"))
        if os.path.isfile(cand):
            data["transcript_path"] = cand
    return data


def clean(text, maxlen=MAXLEN):
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]{1,60}>", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
    if len(text) > maxlen:
        text = text[: maxlen - 1].rstrip() + "…"
    return text


def read_csv(path, header):
    rows = []
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    if not rows:
        rows = [header]
    return rows


def write_csv(path, rows):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)


# -------------------------------------------------------- transcript parsing
def _text_of(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        return "\n".join(c.get("text", "") for c in content
                         if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "text")
    return ""


def is_human_prompt(obj):
    """True for a transcript record that is a prompt typed by the human."""
    if obj.get("type") != "user" or obj.get("isSidechain") or obj.get("isMeta"):
        return False
    msg = obj.get("message") or {}
    content = msg.get("content")
    if isinstance(content, list):
        kinds = {c.get("type") for c in content if isinstance(c, dict)}
        if "tool_result" in kinds:
            return False
    txt = _text_of(content).strip()
    if not txt:
        return False
    # skip hook noise, system-injected turns and interruption markers
    if txt.startswith(("<", "Caveat:", "[Request interrupted")):
        return False
    return True


def parse_transcript(path):
    """Return a dict with turns, timestamps, models, tool counts."""
    turns = []          # list of {"ts", "prompt", "responses": [...], "tools": {...}}
    models, tools = set(), {}
    first_ts = last_ts = None
    version = branch = None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        for line in f:
            try:
                obj = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            ts = obj.get("timestamp")
            if ts:
                first_ts = first_ts or ts
                last_ts = ts
            version = obj.get("version") or version
            branch = obj.get("gitBranch") or branch
            typ = obj.get("type")
            if typ == "user":
                if is_human_prompt(obj):
                    turns.append({"ts": ts, "prompt": _text_of(obj["message"]["content"]).strip(),
                                  "responses": [], "tools": {}})
            elif typ == "assistant" and not obj.get("isSidechain"):
                msg = obj.get("message") or {}
                if msg.get("model"):
                    models.add(msg["model"])
                for c in msg.get("content", []) or []:
                    if not isinstance(c, dict):
                        continue
                    if c.get("type") == "text" and c.get("text", "").strip():
                        if turns:
                            turns[-1]["responses"].append((ts, c["text"].strip()))
                    elif c.get("type") == "tool_use":
                        name = c.get("name", "?")
                        tools[name] = tools.get(name, 0) + 1
                        if turns:
                            turns[-1]["tools"][name] = turns[-1]["tools"].get(name, 0) + 1
    return {"turns": turns, "first_ts": first_ts, "last_ts": last_ts,
            "models": sorted(models), "tools": tools, "version": version,
            "git_branch": branch}


def session_parts(sdir):
    return [p for p in (os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.jsonl"),
                        os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.resumed.jsonl"))
            if os.path.exists(p)]


def parse_session(sdir):
    info = {"turns": [], "first_ts": None, "last_ts": None, "models": set(),
            "tools": {}, "version": None, "git_branch": None, "bytes": 0}
    for p in session_parts(sdir):
        d = parse_transcript(p)
        info["turns"] += d["turns"]
        info["first_ts"] = info["first_ts"] or d["first_ts"]
        info["last_ts"] = d["last_ts"] or info["last_ts"]
        info["models"] |= set(d["models"])
        for k, v in d["tools"].items():
            info["tools"][k] = info["tools"].get(k, 0) + v
        info["version"] = d["version"] or info["version"]
        info["git_branch"] = d["git_branch"] or info["git_branch"]
        info["bytes"] += os.path.getsize(p)
    info["models"] = sorted(info["models"])
    return info


def hhmm(ts):
    return (ts or "")[11:16]


def duration(a, b):
    try:
        fmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"
        mins = int((dt.datetime.strptime(b[:19], fmt)
                    - dt.datetime.strptime(a[:19], fmt)).total_seconds() // 60)
        return f"{mins} min" if mins < 60 else f"{mins // 60} h {mins % 60} min"
    except Exception:
        return "?"


# --------------------------------------------------------- session index csv
def upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=None, first_prompt=None, nprompts=None,
                       branch=None):
    rows = read_csv(SESSIONS_CSV, SESSIONS_HEADER)
    header = rows[0]
    idx = {h: i for i, h in enumerate(header)}
    found = None
    for r in rows[1:]:
        while len(r) < len(header):
            r.append("")
        if r[idx["session_id"]] == sid:
            found = r
    if found is None:
        found = [""] * len(header)
        found[idx["session_id"]] = sid
        found[idx["user"]] = username()
        found[idx["source"]] = source()
        found[idx["topic"]] = "untagged"
        rows.append(found)
    if start_ts and not found[idx["start_date"]]:
        found[idx["start_date"]] = start_ts[:10]
        found[idx["start_time_utc"]] = start_ts[11:19]
    if branch and not found[idx["git_branch"]]:
        found[idx["git_branch"]] = branch
    if first_prompt and not found[idx["first_prompt"]]:
        found[idx["first_prompt"]] = clean(first_prompt, 120)
    if nprompts is not None:
        found[idx["prompts"]] = str(nprompts)
    rows[1:] = sorted(rows[1:], key=lambda r: (r[idx["start_date"]], r[idx["start_time_utc"]]))
    write_csv(SESSIONS_CSV, rows)
    return dict(zip(header, found))


# ------------------------------------------------------------- generators
def write_session_files(sid):
    sdir = os.path.join(LOG, sid)
    info = parse_session(sdir)
    meta_row = upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=info["first_ts"],
                                  first_prompt=(info["turns"][0]["prompt"] if info["turns"] else None),
                                  nprompts=len(info["turns"]), branch=info["git_branch"])
    # session.json
    meta = {
        "session_id": sid,
        "start_utc": info["first_ts"], "last_event_utc": info["last_ts"],
        "span": duration(info["first_ts"], info["last_ts"]),
        "prompts": len(info["turns"]),
        "models": info["models"],
        "tool_use_counts": dict(sorted(info["tools"].items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])),
        "claude_code_version": info["version"],
        "git_branch": info["git_branch"],
        "user": meta_row.get("user"), "source": meta_row.get("source"),
        "topic": meta_row.get("topic"),
        "transcript_files": [os.path.basename(p) for p in session_parts(sdir)],
        "transcript_bytes": info["bytes"],
    }
    with open(os.path.join(sdir, "session.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(meta, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write("\n")
    # prompts.csv
    rows = [["n", "date", "time_utc", "prompt_text"]]
    for i, t in enumerate(info["turns"], 1):
        rows.append([i, (t["ts"] or "")[:10], (t["ts"] or "")[11:19], t["prompt"]])
    write_csv(os.path.join(sdir, "prompts.csv"), rows)
    # PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md
    out = [GENERATED_NOTE, f"# Session `{sid}`", ""]
    out.append(f"- Started (UTC): {info['first_ts'] or '?'}  ")
    out.append(f"- Last event (UTC): {info['last_ts'] or '?'} (span {meta['span']})  ")
    out.append(f"- User: {meta['user']}; source: {meta['source']}; branch: `{info['git_branch']}`  ")
    out.append(f"- Models: {', '.join(info['models']) or '?'}; Claude Code {info['version'] or '?'}  ")
    out.append(f"- Prompts: {len(info['turns'])}; transcript: "
               + ", ".join(meta["transcript_files"]) + f" ({info['bytes'] / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    out.append("")
    out.append("This file is derived from the transcript for readers without an LLM. "
               "Prompts are verbatim; responses are the assistant's text messages "
               "(tool calls and their output are only summarised - see the JSONL for those).")
    out.append("")
    for i, t in enumerate(info["turns"], 1):
        out.append(f"## Prompt {i} - {(t['ts'] or '')[:19].replace('T', ' ')} UTC")
        out.append("")
        out.append("```text")
        out.append(t["prompt"].replace("```", "'''"))
        out.append("```")
        out.append("")
        if t["tools"]:
            used = ", ".join(f"{k} ×{v}" for k, v in sorted(t["tools"].items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))
            out.append(f"_Tools used in this turn: {used}_")
            out.append("")
        out.append(f"### Response {i}")
        out.append("")
        if not t["responses"]:
            out.append("_(no text response recorded - see transcript)_")
        for ts, txt in t["responses"]:
            out.append(f"**[{hhmm(ts)} UTC]**")
            out.append("")
            out.append(txt)
            out.append("")
        out.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(sdir, "PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(out))
    return meta


def write_index():
    sessions = []
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(LOG)):
        sdir = os.path.join(LOG, name)
        if os.path.isdir(sdir) and session_parts(sdir):
            sessions.append((name, write_session_files(name)))
    rows = {r["session_id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(open(SESSIONS_CSV, encoding="utf-8"))} \
        if os.path.exists(SESSIONS_CSV) else {}
    sessions.sort(key=lambda s: s[1]["start_utc"] or "")
    out = [GENERATED_NOTE, "# LLM session log - human-readable index", ""]
    out.append("Every Claude Code session run in this repository is archived here: one "
               "folder per session (named by session id) holding the full transcript, "
               "the prompts as CSV and a readable `PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md`. "
               "`sessions.csv` is the index of sessions and `prompt-log.csv` the "
               "real-time log of every prompt. See `llm-logs/README.md` for the design.")
    out.append("")
    out.append("| Started (UTC) | Topic | Session id | Prompts | Span | Branch | Transcript |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for sid, m in sessions:
        topic = rows.get(sid, {}).get("topic", "untagged")
        out.append(f"| {(m['start_utc'] or '')[:16].replace('T', ' ')} | {topic} | "
                   f"[`{sid[:8]}…`]({sid}/PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md) | {m['prompts']} | "
                   f"{m['span']} | `{m['git_branch'] or ''}` | {m['transcript_bytes'] / 1e6:.1f} MB |")
    out.append("")
    for sid, m in sessions:
        out.append(f"## {(m['start_utc'] or '')[:10]} - `{sid}`")
        out.append("")
        out.append(f"Topic: {rows.get(sid, {}).get('topic', 'untagged')}. "
                   f"Models: {', '.join(m['models']) or '?'}. "
                   f"Tools: " + (", ".join(f"{k} ×{v}" for k, v in list(m['tool_use_counts'].items())[:8]) or "none") + ".")
        out.append("")
        sdir = os.path.join(LOG, sid)
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(sdir, "prompts.csv"), encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
                for r in list(csv.reader(f))[1:]:
                    out.append(f"{r[0]}. {r[2][:5]} - {clean(r[3])}")
        except Exception:
            pass
        out.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(LOG, "SESSIONS.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(out))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- commands
def cmd_session_start(data):
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    if not sid:
        return
    upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=now_utc().strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
                       branch=git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"))


def cmd_prompt(data):
    sid = data.get("session_id", "")
    prompt = data.get("prompt", "")
    if not prompt:
        return
    now = now_utc()
    rows = read_csv(PROMPT_LOG_CSV, PROMPT_LOG_HEADER)
    rows.append([now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), now.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), username(), sid, prompt])
    write_csv(PROMPT_LOG_CSV, rows)
    if sid:
        upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=now.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
                           first_prompt=prompt, branch=git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"))


def cmd_archive(data):
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    tp = data.get("transcript_path")
    if not sid or not tp or not os.path.isfile(tp):
        return
    sdir = os.path.join(LOG, sid)
    os.makedirs(sdir, exist_ok=True)
    dest = os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.jsonl")
    # A session resumed in a fresh container rebuilds a SMALLER (compacted)
    # transcript.  Never clobber a larger archive: write the continuation to
    # transcript.resumed.jsonl instead.  Both files belong to the session.
    if os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.getsize(dest) > os.path.getsize(tp):
        dest = os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.resumed.jsonl")
    shutil.copy2(tp, dest)
    write_index()
    git("add", "llm-logs")


def cmd_commit(data):
    write_index()
    git("add", "llm-logs")
    if git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "--", "llm-logs"):
        git("commit", "-o", "llm-logs", "-m", "llm-logs: archive session log (automatic)")
        branch = git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
        if branch and branch != "HEAD":
            git("push", "origin", f"HEAD:{branch}")


def main():
    import argparse
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("command", choices=["session-start", "prompt", "archive", "commit", "index"])
    ap.add_argument("--session-id")
    ap.add_argument("--transcript")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.command == "index":
        write_index()
        return
    data = read_payload(args)
    {"session-start": cmd_session_start, "prompt": cmd_prompt,
     "archive": cmd_archive, "commit": cmd_commit}[args.command](data)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as exc:  # a hook must never block Claude Code
        sys.stderr.write(f"llmlog: {exc}\n")
    sys.exit(0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""LLM session logger for this repository.

Every Claude Code session that touches this repository is archived under
``llm-logs/<session_id>/`` and indexed in ``llm-logs/sessions.csv``.  This
single script implements all the hook actions so the shell hooks in
``.claude/hooks/`` stay one-liners.

Sub-commands (each reads the Claude Code hook JSON payload on stdin
unless ``--transcript``/``--session-id`` are given explicitly):

  session-start   register the session in sessions.csv (SessionStart hook)
  prompt          append the submitted prompt to prompt-log.csv and to the
                  session's prompts.csv in real time (UserPromptSubmit hook)
  archive         copy the transcript into llm-logs/<session_id>/, rebuild
                  the session's human-readable files and the global index,
                  and ``git add llm-logs`` (Stop + SessionEnd hooks)
  commit          commit ONLY llm-logs/ and push to the current branch
                  (SessionEnd hook)
  index           rebuild llm-logs/SESSIONS.md and every session's
                  PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md from the archived transcripts

Layout of one session folder::

  llm-logs/<session_id>/
      transcript.jsonl              full Claude Code transcript (ground truth)
      transcript.resumed.jsonl      continuation, if the session was resumed
                                    in a fresh container (compacted transcript)
      session.json                  metadata: start/end, models, tools, branch
      prompts.csv                   one row per human prompt (from transcript)
      PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md      every prompt in full and the assistant's
                                    text replies, readable without an LLM

The transcript JSONL is an internal Claude Code format and may change; the
CSV and Markdown files are the stable, human-readable record.  Never edit
the generated files by hand - rerun ``python3 llm-logs/tools/llmlog.py index``.
"""
import csv
import datetime as dt
import getpass
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
LOG = os.path.dirname(HERE)                      # .../llm-logs
ROOT = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or os.path.dirname(LOG)
LOG = os.path.join(ROOT, "llm-logs")
SESSIONS_CSV = os.path.join(LOG, "sessions.csv")
PROMPT_LOG_CSV = os.path.join(LOG, "prompt-log.csv")
SESSIONS_HEADER = ["start_date", "start_time_utc", "session_id", "user",
                   "source", "git_branch", "prompts", "first_prompt", "topic"]
PROMPT_LOG_HEADER = ["date", "time_utc", "user", "session_id", "prompt_text"]
MAXLEN = 200
GENERATED_NOTE = "<!-- generated by llm-logs/tools/llmlog.py - do not edit, rerun `index` -->"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def now_utc():
    return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)


def username():
    return (os.environ.get("PROMPT_LOG_USER")
            or os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL")
            or getpass.getuser())


def source():
    if os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE"):
        return "claude-code-remote"
    return "claude-code"


def git(*args):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, check=False).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""


def read_payload(args):
    """Hook payload from stdin, merged with explicit command-line overrides."""
    data = {}
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        raw = sys.stdin.read()
        if raw.strip():
            try:
                data = json.loads(raw)
            except Exception:
                data = {}
    if args.session_id:
        data["session_id"] = args.session_id
    if args.transcript:
        data["transcript_path"] = args.transcript
    if not data.get("session_id"):
        data["session_id"] = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID", "")
    if not data.get("transcript_path") and data.get("session_id"):
        # Default Claude Code location: ~/.claude/projects/<mangled cwd>/<id>.jsonl
        mangled = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "-", ROOT)
        cand = os.path.expanduser(os.path.join("~", ".claude", "projects", mangled,
                                               data["session_id"] + ".jsonl"))
        if os.path.isfile(cand):
            data["transcript_path"] = cand
    return data


def clean(text, maxlen=MAXLEN):
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]{1,60}>", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
    if len(text) > maxlen:
        text = text[: maxlen - 1].rstrip() + "…"
    return text


def read_csv(path, header):
    rows = []
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    if not rows:
        rows = [header]
    return rows


def write_csv(path, rows):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)


# -------------------------------------------------------- transcript parsing
def _text_of(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        return "\n".join(c.get("text", "") for c in content
                         if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "text")
    return ""


def is_human_prompt(obj):
    """True for a transcript record that is a prompt typed by the human."""
    if obj.get("type") != "user" or obj.get("isSidechain") or obj.get("isMeta"):
        return False
    msg = obj.get("message") or {}
    content = msg.get("content")
    if isinstance(content, list):
        kinds = {c.get("type") for c in content if isinstance(c, dict)}
        if "tool_result" in kinds:
            return False
    txt = _text_of(content).strip()
    if not txt:
        return False
    # skip hook noise, system-injected turns and interruption markers
    if txt.startswith(("<", "Caveat:", "[Request interrupted")):
        return False
    return True


def parse_transcript(path):
    """Return a dict with turns, timestamps, models, tool counts."""
    turns = []          # list of {"ts", "prompt", "responses": [...], "tools": {...}}
    models, tools = set(), {}
    first_ts = last_ts = None
    version = branch = None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        for line in f:
            try:
                obj = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            ts = obj.get("timestamp")
            if ts:
                first_ts = first_ts or ts
                last_ts = ts
            version = obj.get("version") or version
            branch = obj.get("gitBranch") or branch
            typ = obj.get("type")
            if typ == "user":
                if is_human_prompt(obj):
                    turns.append({"ts": ts, "prompt": _text_of(obj["message"]["content"]).strip(),
                                  "responses": [], "tools": {}})
            elif typ == "assistant" and not obj.get("isSidechain"):
                msg = obj.get("message") or {}
                if msg.get("model"):
                    models.add(msg["model"])
                for c in msg.get("content", []) or []:
                    if not isinstance(c, dict):
                        continue
                    if c.get("type") == "text" and c.get("text", "").strip():
                        if turns:
                            turns[-1]["responses"].append((ts, c["text"].strip()))
                    elif c.get("type") == "tool_use":
                        name = c.get("name", "?")
                        tools[name] = tools.get(name, 0) + 1
                        if turns:
                            turns[-1]["tools"][name] = turns[-1]["tools"].get(name, 0) + 1
    return {"turns": turns, "first_ts": first_ts, "last_ts": last_ts,
            "models": sorted(models), "tools": tools, "version": version,
            "git_branch": branch}


def session_parts(sdir):
    return [p for p in (os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.jsonl"),
                        os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.resumed.jsonl"))
            if os.path.exists(p)]


def parse_session(sdir):
    info = {"turns": [], "first_ts": None, "last_ts": None, "models": set(),
            "tools": {}, "version": None, "git_branch": None, "bytes": 0}
    for p in session_parts(sdir):
        d = parse_transcript(p)
        info["turns"] += d["turns"]
        info["first_ts"] = info["first_ts"] or d["first_ts"]
        info["last_ts"] = d["last_ts"] or info["last_ts"]
        info["models"] |= set(d["models"])
        for k, v in d["tools"].items():
            info["tools"][k] = info["tools"].get(k, 0) + v
        info["version"] = d["version"] or info["version"]
        info["git_branch"] = d["git_branch"] or info["git_branch"]
        info["bytes"] += os.path.getsize(p)
    info["models"] = sorted(info["models"])
    return info


def hhmm(ts):
    return (ts or "")[11:16]


def duration(a, b):
    try:
        fmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"
        mins = int((dt.datetime.strptime(b[:19], fmt)
                    - dt.datetime.strptime(a[:19], fmt)).total_seconds() // 60)
        return f"{mins} min" if mins < 60 else f"{mins // 60} h {mins % 60} min"
    except Exception:
        return "?"


# --------------------------------------------------------- session index csv
def upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=None, first_prompt=None, nprompts=None,
                       branch=None):
    rows = read_csv(SESSIONS_CSV, SESSIONS_HEADER)
    header = rows[0]
    idx = {h: i for i, h in enumerate(header)}
    found = None
    for r in rows[1:]:
        while len(r) < len(header):
            r.append("")
        if r[idx["session_id"]] == sid:
            found = r
    if found is None:
        found = [""] * len(header)
        found[idx["session_id"]] = sid
        found[idx["user"]] = username()
        found[idx["source"]] = source()
        found[idx["topic"]] = "untagged"
        rows.append(found)
    if start_ts and not found[idx["start_date"]]:
        found[idx["start_date"]] = start_ts[:10]
        found[idx["start_time_utc"]] = start_ts[11:19]
    if branch and not found[idx["git_branch"]]:
        found[idx["git_branch"]] = branch
    if first_prompt and not found[idx["first_prompt"]]:
        found[idx["first_prompt"]] = clean(first_prompt, 120)
    if nprompts is not None:
        found[idx["prompts"]] = str(nprompts)
    rows[1:] = sorted(rows[1:], key=lambda r: (r[idx["start_date"]], r[idx["start_time_utc"]]))
    write_csv(SESSIONS_CSV, rows)
    return dict(zip(header, found))


# ------------------------------------------------------------- generators
def write_session_files(sid):
    sdir = os.path.join(LOG, sid)
    info = parse_session(sdir)
    meta_row = upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=info["first_ts"],
                                  first_prompt=(info["turns"][0]["prompt"] if info["turns"] else None),
                                  nprompts=len(info["turns"]), branch=info["git_branch"])
    # session.json
    meta = {
        "session_id": sid,
        "start_utc": info["first_ts"], "last_event_utc": info["last_ts"],
        "span": duration(info["first_ts"], info["last_ts"]),
        "prompts": len(info["turns"]),
        "models": info["models"],
        "tool_use_counts": dict(sorted(info["tools"].items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])),
        "claude_code_version": info["version"],
        "git_branch": info["git_branch"],
        "user": meta_row.get("user"), "source": meta_row.get("source"),
        "topic": meta_row.get("topic"),
        "transcript_files": [os.path.basename(p) for p in session_parts(sdir)],
        "transcript_bytes": info["bytes"],
    }
    with open(os.path.join(sdir, "session.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(meta, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write("\n")
    # prompts.csv
    rows = [["n", "date", "time_utc", "prompt_text"]]
    for i, t in enumerate(info["turns"], 1):
        rows.append([i, (t["ts"] or "")[:10], (t["ts"] or "")[11:19], t["prompt"]])
    write_csv(os.path.join(sdir, "prompts.csv"), rows)
    # PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md
    out = [GENERATED_NOTE, f"# Session `{sid}`", ""]
    out.append(f"- Started (UTC): {info['first_ts'] or '?'}  ")
    out.append(f"- Last event (UTC): {info['last_ts'] or '?'} (span {meta['span']})  ")
    out.append(f"- User: {meta['user']}; source: {meta['source']}; branch: `{info['git_branch']}`  ")
    out.append(f"- Models: {', '.join(info['models']) or '?'}; Claude Code {info['version'] or '?'}  ")
    out.append(f"- Prompts: {len(info['turns'])}; transcript: "
               + ", ".join(meta["transcript_files"]) + f" ({info['bytes'] / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    out.append("")
    out.append("This file is derived from the transcript for readers without an LLM. "
               "Prompts are verbatim; responses are the assistant's text messages "
               "(tool calls and their output are only summarised - see the JSONL for those).")
    out.append("")
    for i, t in enumerate(info["turns"], 1):
        out.append(f"## Prompt {i} - {(t['ts'] or '')[:19].replace('T', ' ')} UTC")
        out.append("")
        out.append("```text")
        out.append(t["prompt"].replace("```", "'''"))
        out.append("```")
        out.append("")
        if t["tools"]:
            used = ", ".join(f"{k} ×{v}" for k, v in sorted(t["tools"].items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))
            out.append(f"_Tools used in this turn: {used}_")
            out.append("")
        out.append(f"### Response {i}")
        out.append("")
        if not t["responses"]:
            out.append("_(no text response recorded - see transcript)_")
        for ts, txt in t["responses"]:
            out.append(f"**[{hhmm(ts)} UTC]**")
            out.append("")
            out.append(txt)
            out.append("")
        out.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(sdir, "PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(out))
    return meta


def write_index():
    sessions = []
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(LOG)):
        sdir = os.path.join(LOG, name)
        if os.path.isdir(sdir) and session_parts(sdir):
            sessions.append((name, write_session_files(name)))
    rows = {r["session_id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(open(SESSIONS_CSV, encoding="utf-8"))} \
        if os.path.exists(SESSIONS_CSV) else {}
    sessions.sort(key=lambda s: s[1]["start_utc"] or "")
    out = [GENERATED_NOTE, "# LLM session log - human-readable index", ""]
    out.append("Every Claude Code session run in this repository is archived here: one "
               "folder per session (named by session id) holding the full transcript, "
               "the prompts as CSV and a readable `PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md`. "
               "`sessions.csv` is the index of sessions and `prompt-log.csv` the "
               "real-time log of every prompt. See `llm-logs/README.md` for the design.")
    out.append("")
    out.append("| Started (UTC) | Topic | Session id | Prompts | Span | Branch | Transcript |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for sid, m in sessions:
        topic = rows.get(sid, {}).get("topic", "untagged")
        out.append(f"| {(m['start_utc'] or '')[:16].replace('T', ' ')} | {topic} | "
                   f"[`{sid[:8]}…`]({sid}/PROMPTS-AND-RESPONSES.md) | {m['prompts']} | "
                   f"{m['span']} | `{m['git_branch'] or ''}` | {m['transcript_bytes'] / 1e6:.1f} MB |")
    out.append("")
    for sid, m in sessions:
        out.append(f"## {(m['start_utc'] or '')[:10]} - `{sid}`")
        out.append("")
        out.append(f"Topic: {rows.get(sid, {}).get('topic', 'untagged')}. "
                   f"Models: {', '.join(m['models']) or '?'}. "
                   f"Tools: " + (", ".join(f"{k} ×{v}" for k, v in list(m['tool_use_counts'].items())[:8]) or "none") + ".")
        out.append("")
        sdir = os.path.join(LOG, sid)
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(sdir, "prompts.csv"), encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
                for r in list(csv.reader(f))[1:]:
                    out.append(f"{r[0]}. {r[2][:5]} - {clean(r[3])}")
        except Exception:
            pass
        out.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(LOG, "SESSIONS.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(out))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- commands
def cmd_session_start(data):
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    if not sid:
        return
    upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=now_utc().strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
                       branch=git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"))


def cmd_prompt(data):
    sid = data.get("session_id", "")
    prompt = data.get("prompt", "")
    if not prompt:
        return
    now = now_utc()
    rows = read_csv(PROMPT_LOG_CSV, PROMPT_LOG_HEADER)
    rows.append([now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), now.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), username(), sid, prompt])
    write_csv(PROMPT_LOG_CSV, rows)
    if sid:
        upsert_session_row(sid, start_ts=now.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
                           first_prompt=prompt, branch=git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"))


def cmd_archive(data):
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    tp = data.get("transcript_path")
    if not sid or not tp or not os.path.isfile(tp):
        return
    sdir = os.path.join(LOG, sid)
    os.makedirs(sdir, exist_ok=True)
    dest = os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.jsonl")
    # A session resumed in a fresh container rebuilds a SMALLER (compacted)
    # transcript.  Never clobber a larger archive: write the continuation to
    # transcript.resumed.jsonl instead.  Both files belong to the session.
    if os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.getsize(dest) > os.path.getsize(tp):
        dest = os.path.join(sdir, "transcript.resumed.jsonl")
    shutil.copy2(tp, dest)
    write_index()
    git("add", "llm-logs")


def cmd_commit(data):
    write_index()
    git("add", "llm-logs")
    if git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "--", "llm-logs"):
        git("commit", "-o", "llm-logs", "-m", "llm-logs: archive session log (automatic)")
        branch = git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
        if branch and branch != "HEAD":
            git("push", "origin", f"HEAD:{branch}")


def main():
    import argparse
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("command", choices=["session-start", "prompt", "archive", "commit", "index"])
    ap.add_argument("--session-id")
    ap.add_argument("--transcript")
    args = ap.parse_args()
